versions.short: The bill would amend the existing Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program to continue its work on better ways to measure snowpack and forecast water supply, with a focus on more accurate, timely, and cost-effective snow monitoring technologies. It would add newer methods to the list of approaches the program may explore, such as imaging spectroscopy, machine learning, and snowpack and hydrologic modeling. It would shift the program's focus toward activities that improve forecasts in river basins where they can inform water management and reservoir decisions, including interstate decisions, and toward building the capacity of partners to use these new tools. It would also change the program's reporting requirements to list the basins using these technologies and assess how well new forecasts compare with existing benchmarks from the Department of Agriculture and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Finally, it would set program funding at $3,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
